question: to the Commission Francisco José Millán Mon (PPE) Subject:

The CATCH system aims to be a key tool to strengthen the traceability of fishery products and prevent catches from illegal fishing from entering the EU market. However, almost six months after its implementation, there are still technical issues, delays in the processing of certificates and operational difficulties that are seriously impacting European operators and ports. These shortcomings are causing significant disruption in key European ports, such as the Port of Vigo, the EU’s main fishing port. The industry reports delays in processing imports, logistical backlogs and additional costs (up to EUR 3 000/container) that harm its competitiveness in relation to non-EU operators12. Reports also indicate that the system is not being evenly implemented across Member States, which would compromise the level playing field on the internal market. 1.
Is the Commission aware of these incidents, which continue to affect the functioning of CATCH, and the grave economic impact they have on EU operators and ports?

Is the Commission aware that some Member States are taking national measures to alleviate these difficulties? How does the Commission intend to ensure homogenous application of the rules across the EU?

answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.8.2026) CATCH is operational as of 10 January 2026 and aligned to legal requirements in the revised IUU Regulation1. On 29 July 2026 more than 81 000 valid importer declarations are in CATCH, and no major disruption of trade has been reported to the Commission. CATCH, developed by the Commission together with the Member States, is continuously improved, following confirmation of technical issues or based on feedback from operators and Member States authorities. Eight releases have already taken place since 10 January 2026. Most delays are neither linked to features of CATCH nor to the few new requirements of the revised EU catch certification scheme but to missing or incorrect data in documentation certified by non-EU countries that slow down the submission by EU operators and the validation by Member States authorities. The Commission is making efforts to provide guidance documents and trainings to non-EU countries. These need to be complimented by full enforcement by Member States authorities. 2. The Commission is not empowered to and has hence not granted any derogation to Member States as regards the mandatory use of CATCH and implementation of the revised EU catch certification scheme. The Commission has been carefully monitoring the situation and has engaged with all Member States to ensure the use of CATCH and the relevant submission of data into the system by EU operators. CATCH aims to ensure the harmonisation of IUU import controls. The Commission has provided guidance to Member States to perform checks and verifications.
1 Council Regulation (EC) No 1005/2008 of 29 September 2008 establishing a Union system to prevent, deter

and eliminate illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, amending Regulations (EEC) No 2847/93, (EC) No 1936/2001 and (EC) No 601/2004 and repealing Regulations (EC) No 1093/94 and (EC) No 1447/1999.
